verses.text: “Listen to me, una wey follow after righteousness, una wey seek di Lord. Look to di rock wey dem cut una from, and to di hole of di pit wey dem dig una from.
Look to Abraham una father, and to Sarah wey bear una. Because I call am alone, and I bless am, and make am many.

Because di Lord don comfort Zion. E don comfort all her waste places, and e don make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like di garden of di Lord. Joy and gladness go dey found inside am, thanksgiving, and di voice of melody.
Pay attention to me, my people, and give ear to me, my nation, because law go go out from me, and I go make my justice rest for light of di peoples.
My righteousness dey near. My salvation don go out, and my arms go judge di peoples. Di islands go wait for me, and for my arm dem go trust.

Lift up una eyes to di heavens, and look upon di earth beneath. Because di heavens go vanish away like smoke, and di earth go wear out like garment, and dem wey dwell inside am go die in like manner. But my salvation go be forever, and my righteousness no go dey abolished.
Listen to me, una wey know righteousness, di people wey my law dey for dem heart. No fear di reproach of men, neither dey dismayed at dem insults.
Because di moth go eat dem up like garment, and di worm go eat dem like wool. But my righteousness go be forever, and my salvation to all generations.”
Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of di Lord. Awake, as for di days of old, di generations of ancient times. No be you wey cut Rahab in pieces, wey pierce di dragon?
No be you wey dry up di sea, di waters of di great deep, wey make di depths of di sea way for di redeemed to pass over?
Di ransomed of di Lord go return, and come with singing to Zion. Everlasting joy go dey on dem heads. Dem go obtain gladness and joy. Sorrow and sighing go flee away.
“I, even I, na im comfort una. Who be you, say you dey afraid of man wey go die, and of di son of man wey go be like grass?

You don forget di Lord your Maker, wey stretch out di heavens, and lay di foundations of di earth. You dey fear continually all day because of di fury of di oppressor, as if e ready to destroy. Where di fury of di oppressor dey?
Di captive exile go soon dey freed. E no go die and go into di pit, neither im bread go fail.
But I be di Lord your God, wey stir up di sea so that im waves roar. Di Lord of Armies na im name.
I don put my words for your mouth, and I don cover you for di shadow of my hand, to plant di heavens, and lay di foundations of di earth, and talk to Zion, ‘You na my people.’”
Awake, awake, stand up, Jerusalem, wey don drink from di hand of di Lord di cup of im wrath. You don drink di bowl of staggering to di dregs.
Dey none to guide her among all di sons wey she don bear. Neither dey any wey take her by di hand among all di sons wey she don bring up.
Two things don happen to you. Who go grieve with you? Desolation and destruction, famine and sword. Who go comfort you?
Your sons don faint. Dem lie for di head of all di streets, like antelope for net. Dem full of di wrath of di Lord, di rebuke of your God.
Therefore hear now dis, you afflicted, and drunk, but no with wine:
Your Lord, di Lord, and your God wey dey plead di cause of im people, talk like dis: “See, I don take out of your hand di cup of staggering, di bowl of my wrath. You go no more drink am again.
I go put am into di hand of dem wey afflict you, wey don talk to your soul, ‘Bow down, so that we go go over.’ You don lay your back like di ground, and like di street, to dem wey go over.”
Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion. Put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, di holy city. Because from now on di uncircumcised and di unclean no go enter you again.
Shake yourself from di dust. Arise, sit down, Jerusalem. Loose yourself from di bonds of your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
Because di Lord talk like dis: “Una don sell yourselves for nothing, and una go dey redeemed without money.”
Because di Lord God talk like dis: “My people go down at di first into Egypt to dwell dere. Den di Assyrian oppress dem without cause.
Now therefore wetin I get here,” talk di Lord, “say my people don dey taken away for nothing? Dem wey rule over dem dey howl,” talk di Lord, “and my name continually all di day dey blasphemed.
Therefore my people go know my name. Therefore for dat day dem go know say na I be di one wey talk. See, na me.”
How beautiful upon di mountains be di feet of am wey bring good news, wey publish peace, wey bring good news of good, wey publish salvation, wey talk to Zion, “Your God dey reign!”
Di voice of your watchmen! Dem lift up dem voice. Together dem sing, because dem go see eye to eye, when di Lord return to Zion.
Break out into joy, sing together, una waste places of Jerusalem, because di Lord don comfort im people. E don redeem Jerusalem.
Di Lord don bare im holy arm for di eyes of all di nations. All di ends of di earth don see di salvation of our God.
Depart, depart, go out from dere. Touch no unclean thing. Go out from di middle of am. Make una clean, una wey carry di vessels of di Lord.
Because una no go go out in haste, neither una go go by flight, because di Lord go go before una, and di God of Israel go be una rear guard.
See, my servant go deal wisely. E go dey exalted and lifted up, and go be very high.
Like how many dey astonished at you (im face dey so marred more than any man, and im form more than di sons of men),
so e go sprinkle many nations. Kings go shut dem mouths at am, because wetin dem no dey told, dem go see, and wetin dem no hear, dem go consider.
Who don believe our message? To who di arm of di Lord don dey revealed?
Because e grow up before am like tender plant, and like root out of dry ground. E get no form nor majesty. When we see am, no beauty dey, say we for desire am.
Men despise and reject am, man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief. Like one from whom men hide dem face, e dey despised, and we no esteem am.
Surely e don bear our griefs, and carry our sorrows. Yet we consider am stricken, struck by God, and afflicted.
But e dey wounded for our transgressions. E dey bruised for our iniquities. Di punishment wey bring us peace dey on am, and by im stripes we dey healed.
All we like sheep don go astray. Everyone don turn to im own way, and di Lord don lay on am di iniquity of us all.
E dey oppressed, yet when e dey afflicted e no open im mouth. As lamb wey dem dey lead to di slaughter, and as sheep wey dey silent before im shearers, so e no open im mouth.
By oppression and judgment e dey taken away. As for im generation, who think say e dey cut off out of di land of di living for di disobedience of my people to whom di stroke belong?
Dem make im grave with di wicked, and with di rich im tomb, although e no do violence, neither any deceit dey for im mouth.
Yet na di Lord pleasure to bruise am. E don put am to grief. When you make im soul offering for sin, e go see im offspring. E go prolong im days, and di pleasure of di Lord go prosper for im hand.
After di suffering of im soul, e go see am and dey satisfied. By im knowledge my righteous servant go justify many, and e go bear dem iniquities.

Therefore I go divide am portion with di great, and e go divide di plunder with di strong, because e pour out im soul to death, and dem count am with di transgressors. Yet e bear di sin of many, and make intercession for di transgressors.
“Sing, barren one, you wey no bear. Break out into singing, and cry aloud, you wey no travail, because di children of di desolate pass di children of di married woman,” talk di Lord.
“Enlarge di place of your tent, and make dem stretch out di curtains of your habitations. No hold back. Lengthen your cords, and strengthen your stakes.
Because you go break out on di right hand and on di left, and your offspring go possess di nations, and make di desolate cities dey inhabited.
No fear, because you no go dey ashamed. No dey confounded, because you no go dey disgraced. Because you go forget di shame of your youth, and go no more remember di reproach of your widowhood.
Because your Maker na your husband. Di Lord of Armies na im name. Di Holy One of Israel na your Redeemer. Dem go call am di God of di whole earth.
Because di Lord don call you like wife wey dem forsake and grieved for spirit, even wife of youth when dem reject her,” talk your God.
“For small moment I don forsake you, but with great mercies I go gather you.
For overflowing wrath, I hide my face from you for moment, but with everlasting kindness I go have mercy on you,” talk di Lord your Redeemer.
“Dis na like di waters of Noah to me, because as I don swear say di waters of Noah no go go over di earth again, so I don swear say I no go dey angry with you, nor rebuke you.
Because di mountains may depart, and di hills dey removed, but my loving kindness no go depart from you, neither my covenant of peace go dey removed,” talk di Lord wey get mercy on you.
“You afflicted, tossed with storm, and no comforted, see, I go set your stones with beautiful colours, and lay your foundations with sapphires.
I go make your pinnacles of rubies, and your gates of carbuncles, and all your walls of precious stones.
All your children go dey taught by di Lord, and great go be di peace of your children.
For righteousness you go dey established. You go dey far from oppression, because you go no fear, and from terror, because e no go come near you.
See, dem may gather together, but no by me. Whoever gather together against you go fall because of you.
See, I don create di blacksmith wey blow di fire of coals, and bring out weapon for im work. I don also create di waster to destroy.

No weapon wey dem form against you go prosper. Every tongue wey rise against you for judgment you go condemn. Dis na di heritage of di servants of di Lord, and dem righteousness wey come from me,” talk di Lord.
“Hey, everyone wey dey thirsty, come to di waters! Una wey no get money, come, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
Why una dey spend money for wetin no be bread? Why una dey labour for wetin no satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat wetin good, and make your soul delight itself for fatness.
Turn your ear, and come to me. Hear, and your soul go live. I go make everlasting covenant with una, even di sure mercies of David.
See, I don make am witness to di peoples, leader and commander to di peoples.
See, you go call nation wey you no know, and nation wey no know you go run to you, because of di Lord your God, and for di Holy One of Israel, because e don glorify you.”
Seek di Lord while e dey found. Call on am while e dey near.
Make di wicked forsake im way, and di unrighteous man im thoughts. Make am return to di Lord, and e go have mercy on am, and to our God, because e go abundantly pardon.
“Because my thoughts no be una thoughts, neither una ways my ways,” talk di Lord.
“Because as di heavens dey higher pass di earth, so my ways dey higher pass una ways, and my thoughts pass una thoughts.
Because as di rain come down and di snow from heaven, and no return dere, but water di earth, and make am bring forth and bud, and give seed to di sower and bread to di eater,
so my word go be wey go out of my mouth. E no go return to me void, but e go accomplish wetin I please, and e go prosper for di thing wey I send am to do.
Because una go go out with joy, and dem go lead una forth with peace. Di mountains and di hills go break out before una into singing, and all di trees of di field go clap dem hands.
Instead of di thorn bush, di cypress tree go come up. Instead of di brier, di myrtle tree go come up. E go be to di Lord for name, for everlasting sign wey no go dey cut off.”
Di Lord talk like dis: “Keep justice, and do righteousness, because my salvation dey near to come, and my righteousness to dey revealed.
Blessed na di man wey do dis, and di son of man wey hold am fast, wey keep di Sabbath from profaning am, and keep im hand from doing any evil.”
Make di foreigner wey don join imself to di Lord no talk, “Di Lord go surely separate me from im people.” Neither make di eunuch talk, “See, I be dry tree.”
Because di Lord talk like dis: “To di eunuchs wey keep my Sabbaths, and choose di things wey please me, and hold fast to my covenant,
I go give inside my house and within my walls memorial and name better pass sons and daughters. I go give am everlasting name, wey no go dey cut off.
Also di foreigners wey join demselves to di Lord, to serve am, and to love di name of di Lord, to be im servants, everyone wey keep di Sabbath from profaning am, and hold fast to my covenant,

even dem I go bring to my holy mountain, and make dem joyful for my house of prayer. Dem burnt offerings and dem sacrifices go dey accepted on my altar, because my house go dey called house of prayer for all peoples.”
Di Lord God wey gather di outcasts of Israel talk: “I go gather others to am, beside dem wey dem don gather.”
All una animals of di field, come to devour, yes, all una animals for di forest.
Im watchmen dey blind. Dem all dey without knowledge. Dem all dey dumb dogs. Dem no fit bark. Dem dey dream, dey lie down, dey love to slumber.
Yes, di dogs get strong appetites. Dem no know when dem don get enough. Dem na shepherds wey no fit understand. Dem all don turn to dem own way, everyone to im gain, from im quarter.
“Come,” dem talk, “make I bring wine, and make we fill ourselves with strong drink. Tomorrow go be like today, great and very excellent.”
Di righteous perish, and no man lay am to heart. Devout men dey taken away, none considering say di righteous dey taken away from di evil to come.
E enter into peace. Dem rest for dem beds, each one wey waka for im uprightness.
“But come here, una sons of di sorceress, di offspring of di adulterer and di prostitute.
Who una dey mock? Against who una dey open wide di mouth and stick out di tongue? No be una be children of disobedience, offspring of falsehood,
una wey inflame yourselves among di oaks, under every green tree, wey kill di children for di valleys, under di clefts of di rocks?
Among di smooth stones of di valley na your portion. Dem, dem na your lot. Even to dem you don pour drink offering. You don offer meal offering. I go dey comforted for dis things?
On high and lofty mountain you don set your bed. Even dere you go up to offer sacrifice.

Behind di doors and di posts you don set up your memorial, because you don uncover yourself to another pass me, and gone up. You don enlarge your bed, and made covenant with dem. You love dem bed. You look upon nakedness.
You go to di king with oil, and multiply your perfumes. You send your ambassadors far off, and abase yourself even to Sheol.
You dey weary with di length of your way, yet you no talk, ‘E dey hopeless.’ You find di life of your hand, so you no dey faint.
Who you don dey afraid of and fear, say you don lie, and no remember me, nor lay am to your heart? No be say I don dey silent even of long time, and you no fear me?
I go declare your righteousness, and your works, and dem no go profit you.

When you cry, make di collection of your idols deliver you. But di wind go carry dem all away. Vapour go take dem. But di one wey take refuge inside me go possess di land, and go inherit my holy mountain.”
E go talk, “Build up, build up, prepare di way, take up di stumbling block out of di way of my people.”

Because di high and lofty One wey inhabit eternity, wey im name dey Holy, talk like dis: “I dwell for di high and holy place, and also with am wey get contrite and humble spirit, to revive di spirit of di humble, and to revive di heart of di contrite.
Because I no go contend forever, neither I go dey angry always, because di spirit go faint before me, and di souls wey I don make.
For di iniquity of im covetousness I dey angry, and strike am. I hide, and dey angry. E go on backsliding for di way of im heart.
I don see im ways, and I go heal am. I go lead am also, and restore comforts to am and to im mourners.
I create di fruit of di lips: peace, peace, to am wey dey far off, and to am wey dey near,” talk di Lord, “and I go heal am.”
But di wicked dey like di troubled sea, because e no fit rest, and im waters cast up mire and dirt.
“No peace,” talk my God, “for di wicked.”
“Cry aloud. No hold back. Lift up your voice like trumpet. Declare to my people dem rebellion, and to di house of Jacob dem sins.
Yet dem seek me daily, and delight to know my ways, like nation wey do righteousness, and no forsake di ordinance of dem God. Dem ask me of righteous judgments. Dem delight to draw near to God.
‘Why we don fast,’ dem talk, ‘and you no see? Why we don afflict our soul, and you no take notice?’ See, for di day of your fast you find pleasure, and exploit all your labourers.
See, una fast for strife and contention, and to strike with di fist of wickedness. Una no fit fast like una do today, to make una voice dey heard on high.
Na dis kind fast I don choose? Na day for man to afflict im soul? Na to bow down im head like bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under am? Una go call dis fast, and acceptable day to di Lord?
No be dis be di fast wey I don choose: to loosen di bonds of wickedness, to undo di bands of di yoke, to let di oppressed go free, and to break every yoke?
No be to share your bread with di hungry, and bring di poor wey dey cast out to your house? When you see di naked, to cover am, and no hide yourself from your own flesh?
Den your light go break out like di morning, and your healing go spring forth speedily. Your righteousness go go before you. Di glory of di Lord go be your rear guard.
Den you go call, and di Lord go answer. You go cry, and e go talk, ‘Here I dey.’ If you take away from di middle of you di yoke, di pointing of di finger, and speaking wickedly,
and if you give yourself to di hungry, and satisfy di afflicted soul, den your light go rise for darkness, and your obscurity go be like di noonday.
Di Lord go guide you continually, and satisfy your soul for dry places, and make your bones strong. You go be like watered garden, and like spring of water, wey im waters no fail.
Dem wey go be of you go build di old waste places. You go raise up di foundations of many generations. You go dey called di repairer of di breach, di restorer of paths to dwell in.

If you turn away your foot from di Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on my holy day, and call di Sabbath delight, di holy day of di Lord honourable, and honour am, no doing your own ways, nor finding your own pleasure, nor speaking your own words,
den you go delight yourself for di Lord, and I go make you ride on di high places of di earth. I go feed you with di heritage of Jacob your father, because di mouth of di Lord don speak am.”
See, di Lord hand no too short to save, neither im ear heavy, so that e no fit hear.
But your iniquities don separate between una and your God, and your sins don hide im face from una, so that e no go hear.
Because your hands dey defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity. Your lips don speak lies. Your tongue mutter wickedness.
Nobody sue in righteousness, and nobody plead in truth. Dem trust for emptiness, and speak lies. Dem conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity.
Dem hatch cobra eggs, and weave di spider web. Anyone wey eat dem eggs die, and wetin dem crush break out into viper.
Dem webs no go become garments, neither dem go cover demselves with dem works. Dem works na works of iniquity, and act of violence dey dem hands.
Dem feet run to evil, and dem hurry to shed innocent blood. Dem thoughts na thoughts of iniquity. Desolation and destruction dey dem paths.
Dem no know di way of peace. No justice dey dem goings. Dem don make dem crooked paths. Whoever waka inside dem no know peace.
Therefore justice dey far from us, neither righteousness overtake us. We look for light, but see, darkness, for brightness, but we waka for obscurity.
We grope for di wall like blind men. Yes, we grope like dem wey no get eyes. We stumble for noonday as for twilight. Among di vigorous we dey like dead men.
We all growl like bears, and mourn bitterly like doves. We look for justice, but dey none, for salvation, but e dey far from us.
Because our transgressions dey multiplied before you, and our sins testify against us, because our transgressions dey with us, and as for our iniquities, we know dem:
transgressing and denying di Lord, and turning away from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from di heart words of falsehood.
Justice dey turned back, and righteousness stand far off, because truth don stumble for di street, and uprightness no fit enter.
Yes, truth dey lacking, and e wey depart from evil make imself prey. Di Lord see am, and e displease am, say dey no justice.
E see say no man dey, and wonder say no intercessor dey. Therefore im own arm bring salvation to am, and im righteousness sustain am.
E put on righteousness as breastplate, and helmet of salvation on im head. E put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and wrap imself with zeal as cloak.
According to dem deeds, so e go repay, wrath to im adversaries, recompense to im enemies. To di islands e go repay recompense.
So dem go fear di name of di Lord from di west, and im glory from di rising of di sun, because e go come like rushing stream, wey di breath of di Lord drive.
“Di Redeemer go come to Zion, and to dem wey turn from disobedience for Jacob,” talk di Lord.

“As for me, dis na my covenant with dem,” talk di Lord. “My Spirit wey dey on you, and my words wey I don put for your mouth, no go depart out of your mouth, nor out of di mouth of your offspring, nor out of di mouth of your offspring offspring,” talk di Lord, “from now and forever.”
“Arise, shine, because your light don come, and di glory of di Lord don rise on you.
Because see, darkness go cover di earth, and thick darkness di peoples. But di Lord go arise on you, and im glory go dey seen on you.
Nations go come to your light, and kings to di brightness of your rising.
Lift up your eyes all round, and see. Dem all gather demselves together. Dem come to you. Your sons go come from far, and your daughters go dey carried on di hip.
Den you go see and dey radiant, and your heart go thrill and swell with joy, because di abundance of di sea go dey turned to you. Di wealth of di nations go come to you.
Di multitude of camels go cover you, di young camels of Midian and Ephah. All dem from Sheba go come. Dem go bring gold and frankincense, and go proclaim di praises of di Lord.
All di flocks of Kedar go dey gathered together to you. Di rams of Nebaioth go minister to you. Dem go come up with acceptance on my altar, and I go glorify di house of my glory.
Who be dem wey fly like cloud, and like doves to dem windows?

Surely di islands go wait for me, with di ships of Tarshish first, to bring your sons from far, dem silver and dem gold with dem, for di name of di Lord your God, and for di Holy One of Israel, because e don glorify you.
Foreigners go build up your walls, and dem kings go minister to you, because for my wrath I strike you, but for my favour I don have mercy on you.
Your gates go dey open continually. Dem no go dey shut day or night, so that men go bring to you di wealth of di nations, and dem kings dey led with dem.
Because di nation and kingdom wey no serve you go perish. Yes, those nations go dey utterly wasted.
Di glory of Lebanon go come to you, di cypress tree, di pine, and di box tree together, to beautify di place of my sanctuary, and I go make di place of my feet glorious.
Di sons of dem wey afflict you go come bending to you. All dem wey despise you go bow down at di soles of your feet. Dem go call you di City of di Lord, di Zion of di Holy One of Israel.
Whereas you don dey forsaken and hated, so that no man pass through you, I go make you eternal excellency, joy of many generations.
You go also suck di milk of di nations, and go suck di breast of kings. You go know say I, di Lord, na your Saviour and your Redeemer, di Mighty One of Jacob.
For brass I go bring gold, and for iron I go bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron. I go also make your officers peace, and your overseers righteousness.
Violence no go dey heard again for your land, desolation nor destruction for your borders. But you go call your walls Salvation, and your gates Praise.
Di sun no go be your light by day again, neither for brightness di moon go give light to you, but di Lord go be your everlasting light, and your God your glory.
Your sun no go set again, neither your moon go withdraw itself, because di Lord go be your everlasting light, and di days of your mourning go end.
Your people go all dey righteous. Dem go possess di land forever, di branch of my planting, di work of my hands, so that I go dey glorified.
Di least one go become 1,000, and di small one strong nation. I, di Lord, go hasten am for im time.”
